transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because I just can’t seem to keep my mind on one thing lately. At the warehouse, I’ll be trying to do inventory, and a beeper goes off, or a forklift alarm, or somebody moves a pallet nearby, and I lose my place. Then I look back and realize I put the wrong numbers in. It’s been causing problems.
Did you have this same kind of trouble paying attention when you were a child?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember it being a big problem when I was a kid, not like this. I got through school okay, as far as I remember.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things, even when there isn’t an immediate problem?
Not really, no. I mean, I worry about work when I mess something up, but I wouldn’t say I’m worrying all the time about a bunch of different things for no reason.
Did these attention problems start after something particularly stressful happened in your life?

Yeah, kind of. It started about a month ago, around when my husband stopped working outside the home. Our normal routine changed after that, and that’s when I started noticing the attention problems more.
Over the past month, have you been feeling down or depressed?
I’m not really sure. I wouldn’t say I’ve been especially depressed this past month, at least not that I’ve noticed.
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?
I don’t think so. I still do the things I normally like, as far as I’ve noticed. Nothing really stands out that way.
Do the attention problems seem to get worse when you’re thinking about the changes at home since your husband stopped working?

I don’t know if it’s specifically when I’m thinking about the changes at home. It’s more like I just can’t keep my mind on one thing anymore. At the warehouse, if a beeper goes off, or a forklift alarm, or someone moves a pallet nearby, I get pulled off what I’m counting. Then I realize I put the wrong numbers into inventory.
Before age 12, did you often have trouble paying attention or staying organized?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember it being a big issue when I was that young, but it’s hard for me to say for certain now.
Since your husband stopped working, have you been feeling unusually jumpy or easily startled?
Not really, no. I haven’t noticed being especially jumpy or startled more than usual since then.
Since your husband stopped working, have you been having unwanted memories about that change that keep popping into your mind?
No, I wouldn’t say I’m having unwanted memories popping up like that. I think about it sometimes because it affects the house and bills, but it’s not like it just intrudes on me out of nowhere.
Since your husband stopped working, have you been feeling more nervous or on edge?
I mean, I’ve had some stress about it, sure, but I wouldn’t say I’ve been more nervous or on edge than usual. It’s more just practical worries, I guess.
Since your husband stopped working, have the changes at home been hard for you to adjust to?

Yeah, it has been hard to adjust. I’ve noticed it affecting things more than I expected. At work I’ve made some inventory mistakes and had to double-check with my supervisor. And at home, my husband and I have been arguing enough that it feels like we’re kind of walking around each other instead of settling into him being retired.
Do you often feel restless, like you need to keep moving even when you’re supposed to stay still?

Not so much restless like I can’t sit still, but I have been keeping myself really busy. At work I’ve been taking on extra safety-improvement projects, and outside work I’ve been signing up for more art workshops than I normally would. I’ve been making a lot of lists and schedules, like I’m trying to run the whole thing myself.
When you were in elementary school, did teachers or your parents often say you were easily distracted?
I’m not really sure. I don’t remember teachers making a big issue of that, and I don’t think my parents talked about me being especially distracted. It was a long time ago, though.
Outside of work, have you also been having trouble staying focused on everyday tasks at home?

Yes, I have. It’s like I can’t keep my mind on one thing the way I used to. Even at home I start something and then get pulled off by some little noise or something happening around me, and then I lose track of what I was doing. At work it’s been worse, like a beeper or forklift alarm or someone moving a pallet will throw me off, and then I realize I put the wrong numbers into inventory.
When you lose focus, is your mind usually on the changes at home?

Not really on home changes, no. It’s more like anything around me can pull my attention away. At the warehouse, a beeper or forklift alarm, or even someone moving a pallet, can throw me off the count, and then I catch that I’ve put the wrong numbers into inventory.
Before the changes at home last month, did you usually get distracted this easily?

No, not like this. Before, I could usually stay with what I was doing. Lately it’s like any little thing at the warehouse — a beeper, a forklift alarm, someone moving a pallet — pulls me off, and then I realize I’ve entered the wrong inventory numbers.
When you get distracted, do you find yourself thinking about your husband being home and the changes that has caused?

No, not really. It’s not like I’m sitting there thinking about him being home. It’s more that I just can’t keep my mind on one thing. At the warehouse, any little thing—a beeper, a forklift alarm, someone moving a pallet—pulls me off, and then I realize I put the wrong numbers into inventory.
Has this trouble focusing led to problems in your relationship with your husband?

Yes, it has. We’ve been arguing more than usual, and it’s gotten to where it feels like we’re kind of walking around each other at home instead of getting settled into him being retired. And at work I’ve had to check back with my supervisor after I made mistakes on the inventory, so it’s causing problems there too.
Do you find yourself thinking a lot about your husband stopping work?
I don’t know that I’m thinking about it a lot, no. I mean, it’s a change with him being home, but it’s not like that’s running through my mind all day.
